questions.question: Array [4,10,3,5,1] — build a max-heap using bottom-up sift-down. What's the final array?
questions.solutionApproach: n=5, last internal node index=⌊5/2⌋=2 (1-indexed: [4,10,3,5,1]). At index2(10): children idx4(5),idx5(1), 10 already ≥ both, no swap. At index1(4): children idx2(10),idx3(3). 10>4, swap 4↔10 → [10,4,3,5,1]. Now check index2(4)'s new position: children idx4(5),idx5(1). 5>4, swap → [10,5,3,4,1]. Final: [10,5,3,4,1].

questions.question: A max-heap has 100 elements. What is the worst-case number of comparisons to find the minimum element?
questions.solutionApproach: Minimum must be a leaf. Number of leaves = ⌈100/2⌉ = 50. Need to check all 50 leaves, ~49 comparisons to find min among them.
questions.answer: Θ(n) — approximately 49-50 comparisons (must scan all ~50 leaves).

questions.question: Is it TRUE that the second-largest element in a max-heap is always the LEFT child of the root (not the right child)?
questions.solutionApproach: FALSE — second-largest is guaranteed to be ONE of root's two children, but which one (left or right) is not determined by the heap property; it could be either.
questions.answer: FALSE — second-largest is always A child of root, but not specifically the LEFT one.
